title: The Ground Network
subtitle: Stains, gouges and living veins
text: Blood you project that nothing takes lands where you aimed it as a stain: a few millilitres a face. Stains dry from wet to tacky to a brown crust and then wear away; rain and standing water wash them off at once. Hold Absorption on a wet stain to take part of it back up, on an old one to clean it. A gouge is a trench cut into a face with Vascular Dowsing selected. It stays until Absorption fills it in, or until water runs into its cell or is poured onto it and washes it out; rain does not. It does nothing until you project blood into any part of its run: then a pulse runs along every connected cell, up to sixty-four, and the run glows for a while. Hold a catalyst in your off hand as you pulse and it dissolves into the run and gives it a use: glowstone, an incandescent enzyme or an organic prism make real light; coal or a fervent enzyme make it hot enough to smelt what lies on it, catch the campfires it touches and burn up to four furnaces, smokers or blast furnaces beside it that have something to cook, nearest the pulse first; a compass makes the end nearest its place flare; packed ice or a frigid enzyme freeze still water beside it and hold crops back; iron or a ferric enzyme carry dropped items along it toward where you struck; bone meal or a vivacious enzyme feed what grows beside it; ink or an umbral enzyme hide the run and dim the sight of creatures on it. A hot run lights and burns, and a cold run freezes, only for the one whose blood lit it, and only while they are in the same world; with nobody behind it a run still smelts and chills crops, but lights and freezes nothing. A Catalyst Feeder set beside a lit run dissolves one more each time the run would go dark, for fifteen millilitres of the blood of whoever lit the run, so a lit hallway stays lit while it is stocked. With that one away, dead or short of blood it feeds nothing, and it never lights a dark run; that takes blood again.
